name: HONEYWELL INTERNATIONAL INC.
naics_description: OTHER AIRCRAFT PARTS AND AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT MANUFACTURING
brief_text:
Four detectors flagged Honeywell International for statistical anomalies. Benford's law analysis found the leading digits of award amounts deviate significantly from expected frequency, with digit 1 appearing in only 19.5% of transactions versus the expected 30.1%. Modification growth on contract SPE4A122G0014 expanded at a rate 6,857 times the initial value, vastly exceeding the typical 74-fold growth ratio for peer firms in aircraft parts manufacturing. An isolation forest algorithm identified the entity as a multivariate outlier based on its concentration profile. Finally, sole-source awards comprise 91.6% of the entity's portfolio, substantially above the 45.2% median for comparable manufacturers.

The Benford test yielded a Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic of 0.108 with p-value 4.5e-23 across 2,254 transactions. The modification growth z-score reached 6.62 sigmas, indicating extreme deviation. The isolation forest anomaly score was 0.74 on a 0-to-1 scale. Sole-source concentration z-score was 1.19 sigmas, with 2,064 of 2,254 awards issued without competition. Honeywell's lifetime obligated value totals $716.9 million across a single awarding agency.

These statistical signals warrant scrutiny but do not establish fraud. Benford deviations can reflect legitimate business practices in specialized procurement. Honeywell's massive scale, long operating history, and exclusive DoD relationship may naturally produce sole-source awards and concentrated modification patterns. The peer group for aircraft parts manufacturing contains 328 firms of varying sizes, potentially masking legitimate differences in contract structure and customer relationships. Digit-frequency anomalies in large datasets sometimes reflect rounding conventions or contract-bundling practices rather than manipulation.
